title: Erdős 243 state coordinates, periodic iteration, and finite-horizon residue mechanics

concepts.label: product-cleared reciprocal-tail state
concepts.note: The denominator, tail, centered-error, Sylvester-successor, and next-step-defect coordinates used by the exact integer dynamics.

concepts.label: period and phase-drift iteration
concepts.note: Generic iteration laws that propagate a one-period equality or additive drift through any finite number of periods.

concepts.label: forced finite-horizon residue dynamics
concepts.note: The polynomial forced numerator, recursively shrinking modulus, exact survival predicate, and congruence transport through division.

concepts.label: finite-state and open-problem boundary
concepts.note: Definitions and exact finite transports are Lean-checked; they neither construct nor exclude an infinite negative-state orbit and do not settle Erdős 243.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The Erdős 243 integer-state interface uses the Sylvester successor a^2-a+1, denominator update aD, tail update aC-D, centered error D-(a-1)C, and next-multiplier defect aNext-(a^2-a+1). These are exact definitions of the five product-cleared coordinates used by the rigidity proofs.
statement_nodes.engine: Five exact integer-valued definitions exposing the state variables and the Sylvester comparison in one coordinate system.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Product-cleared coordinates for the reciprocal-tail recurrence; no novelty claim is made for naming or defining them.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Definitions alone prove no orbit exists, no centered error vanishes, and no recurrence is eventually Sylvester.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If x(n+h)=x(n), then x(n+t*h)=x(n) for every t. If instead C(n+h)=C(n)+M, then C(n+t*h)=C(n)+t*M for every t. Thus both a period relation and a fixed additive phase drift iterate with an exact closed form.
statement_nodes.engine: Induction on the number of periods, using associativity and distributivity of natural-number addition and multiplication.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary iteration lemmas recorded as explicit proof interfaces.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: These generic laws assume the one-period equality or drift. They do not prove periodicity, produce a phase drift for an Erdős 243 orbit, or exclude an aperiodic negative branch.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: At index n the normalized constant-negative update has forced numerator (n+1)a^2-(n+2)a+(n+3). A horizon of remaining exact divisions is represented by a recursively shrinking modulus, and ForcedSurvives records exactly whether those divisions succeed.
statement_nodes.engine: A polynomial numerator, an ascending-product modulus exposed recursively, and an inductive exact-divisibility predicate.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Finite-state coordinates for the normalized constant-negative search.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: ForcedSurvives describes a fixed finite number of divisions only. Finite survivors exist and do not constitute an infinite orbit.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The forced numerator respects congruence. When two divisible values agree modulo d*m, exact division by the common nonzero factor d makes their quotients agree modulo m; applying this with d=index+2 gives the one-step forced-quotient transport.
statement_nodes.engine: Polynomial congruence compatibility followed by cancellation of an exact common divisor from both values and the modulus.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary modular arithmetic and exact division.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The transport proves residue-class invariance for one finite search step; it neither supplies divisibility nor promotes finite-horizon survival to an infinite orbit.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The exact one-step congruence transport is obtained by applying polynomial compatibility and quotient cancellation to the forced numerator and the first visible factor of the recursive horizon modulus.

The product-cleared coordinates describe one update, while the generic iteration laws package the period and additive-drift hypotheses used later in the negative-periodic branch; the relation asserts no periodicity of an actual orbit.
